_comment: CLAUDE.md §0.9 (docs/plans/2026-09-18-close-feature-gaps.md) -- per-trader constraints, ADDITIONAL to the platform's own rules, that a trader has decided to trade under from their OWN experience. THE single source of truth read by scripts/trader_constraints.py. Distinct from docs/architecture/account-profiles.json (whose rules the ACCOUNT imposes) and docs/architecture/analysis-params.json (the platform's own thresholds, e.g. the 3R min_rr floor): a trader constraint is a further, personal narrowing on TOP of both, never a way to loosen either.
_scope: Every item here may only TIGHTEN the knob it names -- never loosen it, never introduce a new decision path. scripts/trader_constraints.py.overlay() enforces this by construction (max/intersection/OR, never the reverse) and _validate() refuses an authored value that is already on its face a loosening attempt (e.g. a boolean-only-true kind declared false, or a min_rr below the platform floor). A kind not in `_kinds` is refused at import -- an unenforceable constraint must not be able to look enforced.

min_rr.applies_to: OPTS.min_rr (scripts/backtest-methods.py); live: strategy-runner.py step 10 (planned application, see scripts/trader_constraints.py module docstring)
min_rr.tighten: higher only -- overlay() takes max(current, declared); _validate() refuses a declared value below the platform floor (docs/architecture/analysis-params.json project_defined.ict.min_rr.value, read via scripts/trading_env.min_rr())
min_rr.why: a trader who has personally seen the account get chopped up at 3R may decide THEY only take 3.5R+; the platform floor stays the floor for everyone else

sessions.applies_to: the --sessions admission-time gate (scripts/backtest-methods.py simulate()); carried on the overlay result as `_sessions` because OPTS itself has no session key (session gating happens in simulate(), not in scan())
sessions.tighten: narrower only -- overlay() intersects the declared set with whatever is already in force; _validate() refuses a label not in docs/architecture/sessions.json (scripts/sessions.LABELS)
sessions.why: a trader who only trades London/NY hours for a given methodology should not have Asia session losses counted as evidence against a rule they never trade under

types.tighten: subset only -- overlay() intersects with whatever is already in force
types.why: a trader may have decided type-3 (high-volume) Springs are not for them on a given methodology

htf.tighten: true only -- overlay() ORs the declared value in; _validate() refuses a declared `false` (that would be an attempt to turn an already-on filter off, which is a loosen)
htf.why: a trader may require the HTF filter even when the platform's own default configuration has it off

ict_disp.tighten: true only -- same construction as htf
ict_disp.why: a trader who has seen non-displacement MSS candles fail more often for them may require displacement

ict_pd.tighten: true only -- same construction as htf
ict_pd.why: a trader may require the P/D gate even when the platform default configuration has it off

sloped_gate.tighten: true only -- same construction as htf
sloped_gate.why: a trader running the book engine may want sloped structures skipped even when the run's own flags do not

max_trades_per_day.applies_to: an account rule (live step 10 -- CLAUDE.md §33's own per-symbol churn cap is the closest existing rule shape; this platform's backtest engine has no per-day trade-count gate to apply this to yet, so it is validated here and enforced only at the live integration point, not by scripts/backtest-methods.py)
max_trades_per_day.tighten: lower only -- a declared value must be a positive integer; overlay() takes the min of whatever is already in force
max_trades_per_day.why: a trader who over-trades a setup on bad days may cap their own daily count below whatever the account allows

ict.why: personal decision (trader tung, 2026-09-18): the platform's 3R ICT floor still let through setups that felt like a coinflip at 3R exactly; 3.5R is the trader's own, tighter, line.

wyckoff.why: personal decision (trader tung, 2026-09-18): Wyckoff Springs the trader has reviewed outside London/NY morning hours were mostly thin-liquidity noise; restrict Wyckoff entries for this trader to those two sessions.
